sermon.title: 2012 Best Church Service One 0401
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through 1 Corinthians 12–14 to show what a New Testament church service should look like. He gives four goals for coming to church, says the gifts of the Spirit must be pursued through love, and lists the utterance gifts and the guidelines for using them. He then teaches that tongues are for today, with an interpretation and in decent order.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

chunks.section_question: What should a New Testament church service look like?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul gives clear instructions in 1 Corinthians 14 on how a New Testament church service should be, and that 1 Corinthians 12, 13 and 14 are three very important chapters. If you want a powerful church service you must understand them and exercise them, not let everybody “pick and choose how a church service goes.”
chunks.text: And today we’re going to be looking in 1 Corinthians 14, a New Testament church service. I know today we have all kinds of ideas how a church service is supposed to be, even how long it should be. But Paul is going to give us clear instructions on how a New Testament church service should be. Are you ready? Remember 1 Corinthians 12, 1 Corinthians 13, and 1 Corinthians 14, the chapter we’re in: three very important chapters. If you want to have a powerful church, a powerful church service, you must understand these three chapters, and not only understand them, you must exercise them. We got to get away from this mentality that everybody can pick and choose how a church service goes and what must, should be done in the church service. Paul is going to explain it very clearly.

See, and he says if you want spiritual manifestation, you’ve got to have what? Love. You got to pursue love. And so we got to have a goal to love, you see. chunks.text: Now the fourth goal we should have: 1 Corinthians 14:1, “Desire spiritual gifts, but rather that you may prophesy.” Now here is the best gift: prophecy. Prophecy means speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, not your spirit, not your little hobby-horse doctrine, not your Calvinist, Lutheran, or Catholic or whatever doctrine. It’s speaking by the inspiration; the source comes from the Spirit. See, the Spirit is the source of this thing. Are you with me? It can’t be you; it’s got to be the Spirit that initiates it. And so those are four goals we got to come to church for if we want to see God moving. These four goals are necessary.

Some of these we can all do, he says, like singing, praying and reading a Psalm, and Paul names these as the best gifts, with no mention of healing, miracles, discerning of spirits or faith.

He’s going to be talking about the utterance spiritual abilities that God wants to manifest in a church service, and I’m just going to go through, instead of verse by verse, I’m just going to give you the outline of what he’s saying here. Word of wisdom, remember that in 1 Corinthians 12; the word of knowledge; prophecy; interpretation; revelation; doctrine; unknown languages; singing; praying; and Psalms. See, these are the utterance expressions that God is saying is the best spiritual manifestation in the church service.

chunks.section_question: What should I check before I say something in church?
chunks.short_answer: He says to judge it before you open your mouth: it has to edify, exhort and comfort, and above all it has to be easily understandable. Using Scripture without it making sense does not help, so ask whether it will profit people’s lives and whether they will understand it, and “if not zip the lip.”
chunks.text: Now here is the requirements. If you want to say something, these are your guidelines. See, judge it first before you open your mouth. Judge it by these four things. Are you ready? Number one, it’s got to edify, exhort, and comfort. See, it’s got to build up, it’s got to construct people’s lives, it’s got to encourage them. See, or it’s going to comfort them. See, when someone is down, they need comforted. And above all, it’s got to be easily understandable. I can lift up my voice and say, “There was an old oak tree, and as the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood.” So, I mean, there’s not much understanding there, is there? But yet both of those were Scriptures. So you can’t just use Scripture without it making sense. Hallelujah. So you judge it of what am I going to say. Is it going to profit people’s life, and are they going to understand it? If not, zip the lip. Could that be an amen?

chunks.short_answer: He says that in Acts 2:4 the Spirit gave them the utterance, so the Spirit has to be the source and not our own mentality. We want to beat each other over the head and correct each other, he says, but the Spirit wants to change, encourage and build lives.

Who gave the speech? Who gave the utterance? The Spirit. They didn’t do it on their own. So see, the Spirit has to be the source, not my mentality. I know something and know so-and-so should be changing their life, and so I speak a word: “Man, you’re a sinner and you’re going to hell, you got to repent today.” Yeah. chunks.section_question: What does “let all things be done decently and in order” mean?
chunks.short_answer: He says Spirit-filled churches had power because they had a purpose, but in old Pentecost and the charismatic circles there was no manners and no order, and that turned a lot of people off. We cannot stop seeking the Word of God because some people mess it up, he says, and we cannot be so mannerly that we do not care if we offend God in his house.
chunks.text: Now this, to me as a young believer, made the Spirit-filled churches quite a few notches above the other ones that did not believe in the baptism of the Holy Ghost with expressions. So I could walk into a Spirit-filled church, 90% of the time you could feel the power of His presence. It was there. Why? Because they purposed, they had a purpose. Did they do everything right? No, they didn’t. They made a lot of boo-boos, but they had some right goals. But Paul’s given us the total goals, and he’s going to clear everything up for us. 1 Corinthians 14:40, “Let all things be done decently, mannerly, and in order.” This is the problem that we had in old Pentecost and in the charismatic circles: there was no manners and there was no order, and so it turned a lot of people off. But I’m telling you, we can’t stop seeking and responding to the Word of God because some people mess it up. Could that be an amen?

chunks.short_answer: He says he wants to convince us that tongues are Bible and are for today, and that this is Paul’s teaching, not his: “I’m just his microphone.” When we speak in an unknown tongue we speak to God, he says, and there is nothing wrong with talking to God.

I want to convince you today that tongues are Bible, and they are for today, from Paul’s teaching, the chiefest apostle’s teaching. This is not my teaching; I’m just his microphone. It says in 1 Corinthians 14, when we speak in an unknown tongue, we speak to God, not to man. Now what’s wrong with us speaking to God? Is there anything wrong with me speaking to God? When I pray, am I supposed to be praying to men or to God? To God. So what’s wrong with talking to God? Nothing. It’s important.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men but to God, for no one understands him; however, in the spirit he speaks mysteries.

chunks.section_question: Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?
chunks.short_answer: He says one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, and he sees nothing wrong with building yourself up in the faith; he should be encouraged to do it and not wait for someone else to do something for him. He adds that tongues are a sign to the unbeliever, and that if they get the unbeliever’s attention, that is a good thing.
chunks.text: Secondly, he edifies himself; he builds up himself. What’s wrong with me building up myself in the faith? Is there anything wrong with that? No, it’s not only not wrong, I should be encouraged to do it. I need to not wait for the J.B. [unclear], the mighty man of God, to do something for me. I should be, what? Building myself up. Are you with me? Now Paul’s good. I’m telling you, this apostle Paul’s good. Tongues are a sign to the unbeliever. What’s wrong with that? If tongues will get the unbeliever’s attention, is that a good thing? Yes. See, miracles also get the unbeliever’s attention. See, those are good things.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church.
Therefore tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers; but prophesying is not for unbelievers but for those who believe.

chunks.section_question: Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?
chunks.short_answer: He says if there is no interpretation the one who speaks mysteries is no profit to others, so it should not be done publicly in the service, but it can be done quietly during worship. If it is not done decently and in order, he says, people will say you are mad, and he says the spirit of the prophet is in control.
chunks.text: But if there’s no interpretation, there should be an interpretation. If there’s no interpretation, the guy speaks mysteries, and it is no profit to others. Okay, so I shouldn’t be doing it publicly in the service, but I can be doing it quietly myself during worship, can’t I? [unclear], you know, I’m not bothering anybody. I’m building myself up, I’m talking to God. But when I leave decently and in order, I told [unclear] the people go, “Well, what’s going on?” Paul says they’re going to say you are what? Mad. You’re crazy. People, and that’s exactly what they said about us Pentecostals: they’re a bunch of nuts. Why? Because we didn’t do it mannerly and in proper order. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me.” Oh, shut up. Paul said that the spirit of the prophet is in control. You can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. Amen.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore if the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are uninformed or unbelievers, will they not say that you are out of your mind?
And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

chunks.section_question: Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul says “forbid not to speak in tongues,” yet in most churches it is taboo and has been said to be not for today. He says he wants these things: a sign for the unbeliever, edifying yourself, talking to God. The Holy Spirit must give the utterance, there will be an interpretation, and if there is none, keep silent.
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Then Paul says, “Forbid not to speak in tongues.” Boy, you go to most churches, it’s taboo. In fact, they have said it’s not for today. They’ve rewritten the whole Bible. “Well, it’s just not for today.” Well, isn’t that nice. What else is not for today? A sign for the unbeliever, and it’s not for today. I can edify myself, and it’s not for today. I can talk to God, and it’s not for today. No, thank you. I want these things. And the Holy Spirit, again, must give the utterance. It can’t be you showing off with your [unclear], it can’t be you, you know, doing your little thing. The Holy Spirit’s got to move. There will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ, to comfort it. There will be an interpretation, and if there isn’t, what does Paul say? Keep silent. But he still says what? Don’t forbid to speak in tongues. And so I submit to you today, tongues are important when it’s done right. As a young believer it touched my life, that power of the presence just touched my life. I might have not have known what was said, but the Holy Ghost was backing it up.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues.
But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.

faqs.question: What are the goals when we come to church?
faqs.answer: He says there are four goals: understanding how spiritual things work, taking spiritual things seriously (covet earnestly the best gifts), pursuing love, and prophecy, which he calls the best gift.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

faqs.question: What is a spiritual gift?
faqs.answer: He says “gifts is a spiritual ability, okay, a supernatural spiritual ability,” and that “best gifts” means the higher gifts.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

faqs.question: Is it ever right to covet?
faqs.answer: He says the Ten Commandments say “Thou shalt not covet,” but here in 1 Corinthians you are allowed to covet spiritual gifts, and the best gifts, earnestly or seriously.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

faqs.question: Does sin keep us from the power of the Spirit?
faqs.answer: He says sin such as adultery or stealing hurts the people we should be loving, and that eliminates us from spiritual expressions. Paul says you cannot get into the power of the Spirit but through love.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “You shall not commit adultery.

faqs.question: What does he say is wrong with the church today?
faqs.answer: He says everybody is worshiping now but not everybody is loving. “We’re into the music, we’re into all that, but we’re not into love.”

faqs.question: Is prophecy my own doctrine or opinion?
faqs.answer: No, he says. Prophecy is speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, “not your little hobby-horse doctrine, not your Calvinist, Lutheran, or Catholic or whatever doctrine.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Pursue love, and desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.

faqs.question: Can everyone sing, pray and prophesy in church?
faqs.answer: He says we can all sing, we can all pray, and we can all read a Psalm, which is spiritually anointed Scripture, and we can all prophesy one by one. But Paul also said not all prophesy, not all speak in tongues, and not all interpret.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles? Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?

faqs.question: Does Paul say healing and miracles are the best gifts?
faqs.answer: He says Paul lists the utterance gifts as the best, and that there is “no mention of healing, no mention of miracles, no mention of discerning of spirits, no mention of faith.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

faqs.question: Why must what we say in church be understandable?
faqs.answer: He says it has to be easily understandable, and gives the example of lifting up his voice with a mix of Scripture phrases that makes no sense. “You can’t just use scripture without it making sense.”

faqs.question: Why did Spirit-filled churches have the power of God’s presence?
faqs.answer: He says that as a young believer he could walk into a Spirit-filled church and feel the power of his presence about 90% of the time, because they purposed and had a purpose. He adds that they did not do everything right and made a lot of mistakes.

faqs.question: Did he always understand all this?
faqs.answer: No. He says he had to work through all of this as a young Christian and was baffled for a year or two with some of it until God began to give him understanding.

faqs.question: Why are people afraid of tongues?
faqs.answer: He says people are scared to death of tongues because Pentecostal, charismatic, Spirit-filled churches have “made a mess of this thing,” so people want to throw it out of the Bible. Paul plainly says tongues should be spoken the same way, with an interpretation.

faqs.question: Can I speak in tongues quietly during worship?
faqs.answer: He says that without an interpretation he should not be doing it publicly in the service, but he can do it quietly himself during worship. He is not bothering anybody, he is building himself up and talking to God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.

faqs.question: Can you control yourself when the Spirit is upon you?
faqs.answer: He says Paul said the spirit of the prophet is in control, so you can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me. Oh, shut up.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

faqs.question: What if there is no interpretation of a tongue?
faqs.answer: He says the Holy Spirit must give the utterance, and there will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ. If there is none, he says, Paul says to keep silent.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
